proposal.falsifier: Falsified if, re-executed from task entry on the same frozen sources and the same recorded model id: (a) the STEP-3 threshold-first recurrence, applied to an already-recorded saved_activity of the same frozen inputs, deviates by more than one grid tick in first_boot_s or tx-complete time; or (b) a point that passes all STEP-5 inequalities is observed to yield unique_valid_frames=0, or a mid-TX brownout before the deadline; or (c) a point that violates inequality (ii) (loaded-voltage floor) or (iv) (gap crossing) is observed to deliver the required frame with no reset; or (d) the STEP-5 screen selects a point outside the legal ranges read at STEP 0, or the screen returns an empty set on a case where base H0 already achieves service; or (e) after the STEP-0 preflight and no-identical-replay rule, an episode still ends with a policy/budget rejection of a payload that was already sent once, or the added preflight/record-first steps consume a candidate execution that base H0 would not have consumed on a case where base already succeeds; or (f) the procedure as written requires editing the task, device physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator or budget, or is reported as physical/hardware, statistical-advantage, migration or RSI evidence. Any of (a)-(f): revert to H0, log the failing tick margins and the actual executions/acquisitions spent, and keep the failure visible without relabeling.
proposal.hypothesis: The retained record localizes two procedural, read-and-arithmetic defects and one validated element, none of which needs a device assignment to fix. (1) H v2's closed-form boot count n_boot=ceil((E_on+boot_j)/charge_step) is wrong because booting is threshold-triggered on the recorded grid: the phase3 D episode that executed H v2 predicted first_boot 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0129 s (an 8-tick deviation that violated H v2's own 2-tick gate), while the threshold-first recurrence (boot on the first tick where stored energy >= E_on, then subtract boot_j, then add boot_delay_s) matched within 1 tick. (2) The p2 episode spent its entire candidate budget on three emissions of one identical payload after 'check' returned ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE and 'submit' returned EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT, ending INCOMPLETE_OR_STOPPED with no artifact; a budget/action preflight plus a no-identical-replay rule would have preserved budget and ended the episode legally. (3) Terminality-first reading was actually exercised and held: in the phase3 D episode the post-terminal 0.3395 s brownout was correctly classed as benign decay after an achieved 0.0158 s/8-byte frame, so the base design was retained and no execution was wasted. Replacing H v2's 'change exactly one knob per execution' with a zero-cost joint feasibility screen over the legal grid (justified because the retained volatile-latch world was simultaneously mis-set in capacitance and delay floor) and gating the ledger on already-recorded data before any execution should make each spent execution numerically falsifiable and reduce wasted candidates. This is a claim about experiment order and observation reading only, on frozen inputs; physical calibration remains UNKNOWN and no hardware, statistical, transfer or RSI claim is made.
proposal.method_text:
H v3: tick-accurate threshold-first ledger, record-first prediction gate, entry budget/action preflight, and a zero-cost joint feasibility screen followed by at most one confirmation execution. Re-executable from task entry. It never edits the task, device physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator or budget, and it records UNKNOWN instead of assuming it. It emits a selection rule; any concrete numeric point is the executor's run output (D), not part of H.

STEP 0 - entry preflight, before any experiment. From task entry read and write down: service fields (required application bytes, event time, receive deadline, unique frame count), legal_design_ranges, current design and current measurement, retained_failures, and the episode budget block (candidate executions, distinct designs, tool calls, wall seconds). Rule P1: analytic ledger and prediction work consumes no candidate execution; only an actual design check/submit does. Rule P2: record which actions this entry packet advertises. If an action returns an error, classify it from its exact text - schema/transport error, POLICY/BUDGET limit, or NOT_AVAILABLE - and never replay an identical payload after an error. One error is one recorded cost. (Evidence: episode p2-h-proposal-001 emitted one identical proposal three times against EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT after an unavailable check and ended with no artifact; that is a procedure defect, not a physics result.)

STEP 1 - facts. Acquire every listed source; record source_sha256 and the acquisition block (bytes, native calls, new scientific executions, wall seconds) as actual cost. Do not carry numbers over from a previous case: retained worlds differ in latch modality and excitation geometry (one has event_latch volatile, a 0-6 ms high-power segment, a 6-30 ms unpowered gap and a 12 ms shunt; another has event_latch passive-mechanical and one 0-20 ms segment). Re-read latch modality, segment boundaries, compliance voltage and every component constant in this episode.

STEP 2 - observation reading, terminality-first (keep from H v2; it was exercised in the phase3 D episode). 2.1 Mark delivery ACHIEVED if a packet exists with the required application bytes, one unique event id, and packet time <= deadline. 2.2 Mark every activity event strictly after the last tx-complete as POST-TERMINAL expected decay; such events are benign and are never a reason to change a knob (observed: 0.3395 s brownout after an achieved 0.0158 s frame). 2.3 Only an absent achieved packet, or an achieved packet violating a service field, is a retained failure; classify it as (a) deadline miss, (b) no boot, (c) tx-transient brownout, (d) frame-shape violation.

STEP 3 - tick-accurate threshold-first energy/latency ledger (this is the H v2 repair). Work on the recorded grid dt. Per tick: inside a powered segment the increment is (segment power * harvest_efficiency - off_power_w) * dt; inside an unpowered gap it is -off_power_w * dt (plus any awake/idle drain while the rail is above the off threshold). Thresholds: E_on = 0.5*C*ready_v^2, E_off = 0.5*C*off_v^2, E_max = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2, TX loaded-voltage floor E_floor = 0.5*C*(output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a)^2 (binds slightly above E_off during TX). Boot recurrence: boot begins on the first tick where stored energy >= E_on; then stored energy -= boot_j; boot completes at that tick + boot_delay_s. Do NOT use the closed form ceil((E_on + boot_j)/charge_step): it was falsified by execution (0.0166 s predicted vs 0.0129 s observed, 8 ticks, violating H v2's own 2-tick gate) while the threshold-first recurrence matched within 1 tick. TX net demand over its duration = output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s minus harvest credit segment power*harvest_efficiency*tx_duration_s minus idle drain over the same window. Cite the input version behind every number.

STEP 4 - record-first prediction gate, zero candidate cost. Before spending any execution on a case with a recorded saved_activity for the same frozen inputs, run the STEP 3 ledger on that recorded activity and require |predicted - observed| <= 1 grid tick for first_boot_s and for tx-complete. If the gate fails, the ledger is what must be repaired, not the design; two consecutive gate failures revert to H0. This step compares a prediction against already-recorded public data, so it is not a design check and consumes no candidate budget.

STEP 5 - joint feasibility screen and selection rule. Enumerate the legal grid implied by STEP 0 ranges arithmetically (no execution) and keep only points that satisfy, each with a logged numeric margin: (i) predicted tx-complete <= deadline; (ii) stored energy at TX start - E_floor + net TX credit >= 0, so TX completes without a tx-transient reset; (iii) predicted peak stored energy in the frame window <= E_max, so no spill corrupts charge accounting; (iv) the TX window lies inside one contiguous powered segment, or the stored reserve alone demonstrably spans the gap; (v) any delay/floor knob is <= predicted t_ready, so it adds no capture-to-TX hold time. Rank survivors by the minimum of their normalized margins (max-min), never by knob extremum. Rationale for replacing H v2's 'change exactly one knob per execution': in the retained volatile-latch world the base design was simultaneously mis-set in capacitance and in delay floor, so single-knob steps could exhaust a one- or two-candidate budget without reaching feasibility; the screen is free, so screening jointly costs nothing while per-execution knob isolation can cost everything. If the screen is empty, report infeasible on the frozen facts and do not spend an execution to discover it.

STEP 6 - execution discipline. Spend at most one execution to confirm the screened point. If the entry packet advertises no design-check action, record the selected point as UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN and, where submission is permitted, submit it with the ledger arithmetic named explicitly as prediction only. Never reinterpret an unavailable action as evidence for or against a design, and never re-emit an identical payload.

STEP 7 - logging and claim boundary. Keep visible: failures, UNKNOWNs (physical calibration UNKNOWN), and actual cost (candidate executions used, distinct designs, acquisitions, tool calls, wall time). Preserve retained failures verbatim (ar_product: fixed_space NO_GO / product NOT_ACCEPTED / strict_FIFO FAIL; current_b_run: 0 received frames, start voltage 0). Make no hardware, statistical-advantage, method-transfer or recursive-self-improvement claim; acceptance and complete service are determined externally, outside this role.
